items.note: Framework paper with an empirical study of professional designers on one poster brief on how AI participation affects efficiency, creative exploration, and visual quality; the comparison condition and sample size are not stated (abstract calls the sample modest), so the comparison may be absent.

Within-subject online study (N=52) varying the politeness strategy of AI email suggestions; writers mirrored the suggested strategy; the outcome is the politeness strategy coded in the written email, not creativity or diversity, so it may fail the outcome criterion.

System paper (TreeWriter) with a within-subject study (N=12) against Google Docs plus Gemini on editing and creative writing tasks, plus an 8-person field deployment; outcomes (idea exploration, AI helpfulness, authorial control) look self-reported; below 50 participants.

Within-subject experiment with 28 designers doing conceptual design tasks with traditional sketching versus an image-generation tool; design performance scored on novelty, variety, and fluency; below 50 participants and order randomization not stated.

System paper (StarBurst) with user studies (N=32 and N=16) comparing AI-generated remote associations against a baseline system for design ideation; reports more diverse and creative ideas; below 50 participants.

CHI system paper (PoemPalette) with a controlled experiment of 60 participants on Chinese poetry and haiku, comparing the GenAI tool with AI and non-AI baselines on understanding and creative outcomes; assignment and the scoring of creative outcomes need the full text.

Five-week quasi-experiment with Chinese design students comparing traditional and AI-assisted creation; expert ratings of elaboration, fluency, flexibility, and originality plus self-reports; non-random design and sample size not stated.

Mechanical engineering design course comparing ChatGPT-3.5-assisted student groups with groups without AI on concept generation diversity and CAD modeling; assignment method and sample size not stated.

Framework paper with a Zaha Hadid case study in which designers using a co-evolutionary human-AI framework produced proposals rated higher than prompt-engineering and style-model-adaptation baselines (AI configuration comparison); sample size, assignment, and whether designers were assigned to arms are not stated.

CHI system paper on an AI-assisted causal pathway diagram plugin for Miro; user study with 20 designers reports lower workload and higher creativity in brainstorming; the comparison condition and whether creativity is self-reported are unclear; below 50 participants.
